cards.headline: EFCC re-arraigns ex-Skye Bank chair Tunde Ayeni on N15.6bn fraud charges
cards.what_happened: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has re-arraigned Tunde Ayeni, a former chairman of Skye Bank, on fraud charges totalling N15.6bn. The re-arraignment concerns alleged fraud linked to a former bank chair, a matter of corporate governance accountability in Nigeria's banking sector.
key_facts: EFCC re-arraigned ex-Skye Bank chair Tunde Ayeni.
analysis: As reported by Premium Times; AURA has not checked court or agency records. An allegation or charge is not a finding of guilt.

cards.headline: Senate summons NCC, MTN, Airtel, others over poor network, unjustified airtime deductions
cards.what_happened: The Nigerian Senate has summoned the Nigerian Communications Commission and major telecom operators, including MTN, Airtel, Globacom and T2, over persistent network failures and alleged unjustified airtime deductions. A Senate Committee on Communications, chaired by Ikra Bilbis, has been mandated to investigate subscriber losses and report back within four weeks.
key_facts: The motion was sponsored by Tahir Monguno (APC, Borno North), the Senate Chief Whip.
The motion was presented by Lola Ashiru (APC, Kwara South), the Deputy Majority Leader.

cards.headline: Mambilla project: Imoke insists contract award to Sunrise was invalid
cards.what_happened: Cross River State Governor Ben Ayade's predecessor-era opposition figure Imoke has insisted that the award of the Mambilla power project contract to Sunrise was invalid. The dispute centres on the validity of the contract award for the Mambilla hydropower project in Taraba State.
key_facts: Imoke insists the contract award to Sunrise for the Mambilla project was invalid.
analysis: Why it matters: A public challenge to the validity of a major hydropower contract award raises questions about procurement process and accountability for public money in Nigeria's power sector.

cards.headline: Weak oversight, market gaps stall power tariff reforms
cards.what_happened: Power tariff reforms in Nigeria are reported to be stalled by weak regulatory oversight and market gaps. The article's text is limited to its headline, so no further details on the parties, figures or timelines are available.
